The central `toevah-abomination-cross-corpus-keyword` `appliesTo` is extended to GEN-WOH-47:3 to capture this Gen 46:34 / 47:3 narrative-link; the existing rationale already documents the chapter-46 *to'evah* in the Egyptian-evaluator sense (Vergote, Redford, Bietak, Hoffmeier Hyksos-period scholarship).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֗ה לָג֣וּר בָּאָרֶץ֮ בָּאנוּ֒ כִּי־אֵ֣ין מִרְעֶ֗ה לַצֹּאן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לַעֲבָדֶ֔יךָ כִּֽי־כָבֵ֥ד הָרָעָ֖ב בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וְעַתָּ֛ה יֵֽשְׁבוּ־נָ֥א עֲבָדֶ֖יךָ בְּאֶ֥רֶץ גֹּֽשֶׁן׃

i18n.en: And they said unto Pharaoh, To sojourn in the land are we come; for there is no pasture for thy servants' flocks; for the famine is sore in the land of Kena'an: now therefore, we pray thee, let thy servants dwell in the land of Goshen.

notes.official: *La-gur ba-aretz banu* — 'to sojourn in the land are we come.' The verb *gur* (root g-w-r) is the patriarchal-sojourner self-designation of Genesis, saturating the corpus from Avraham's Mitsrayim-descent (Gen 12:10) through to this chapter (cross-corpus Gen 17:8 *eretz megurekha*; 20:1 *va-yagar bi-Grar*; 21:23+34; 23:4 *ger ve-toshav anokhi immakhem*; 26:3; 28:4; 32:5; 35:27; 36:7; 37:1 *eretz megurei aviv*; here at 47:4, 9). The new central `megurim-patriarchal-sojourner-self-identity-gur-root` governs the verb-and-noun cluster across the cycle as a major cross-corpus theological-self-designation. Named scholarship: Brueggemann's *The Land* on the land-promise-as-not-yet; Westermann on the *ger* legal-status; von Rad on *gur* as theological self-designation; the cross-corpus Heb 11:13 NT-citation of v 9 as the *xenoi-kai-parepidemoi* register. ASV-baseline 'sojourn' preserved.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֔ה אֶל־יוֹסֵ֖ף לֵאמֹ֑ר אָבִ֥יךָ וְאַחֶ֖יךָ בָּ֥אוּ אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: And Pharaoh spake unto Yosef, saying, Thy father and thy brethren are come unto thee:

paragraphs.text: אֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ לְפָנֶ֣יךָ הִ֔וא בְּמֵיטַ֣ב הָאָ֔רֶץ הוֹשֵׁ֥ב אֶת־אָבִ֖יךָ וְאֶת־אַחֶ֑יךָ יֵשְׁבוּ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ גֹּ֔שֶׁן וְאִם־יָדַ֗עְתָּ וְיֶשׁ־בָּם֙ אַנְשֵׁי־חַ֔יִל וְשַׂמְתָּ֛ם שָׂרֵ֥י מִקְנֶ֖ה עַל־אֲשֶׁר־לִֽי׃

i18n.en: the land of Mitsrayim is before thee; in the best of the land make thy father and thy brethren to dwell; in the land of Goshen let them dwell: and if thou knowest any able men among them, then make them rulers over my cattle.

notes.official:
Pharaoh implements the Gen 45:18 grant: *be-meitav ha-aretz* — 'in the best of the land' — governed by the existing overlay `chelev-ha-aretz-best-of-the-land-pharaoh-grant-gen45`, here extended to GEN-WOH-47:6 + 47:11 as the grant's narrative-fulfilment.

The new overlay `anshei-chayil-able-men-office-title-gen47` documents the *anshei chayil* office-title — 'men of valor / able men / capable men.' Cross-corpus the construction is an office-title for administrative or military leadership (Exod 18:21+25, the judges-appointment criterion under Yitro's counsel; Deut 3:18; Judg 11:1 Yiftach; 1 Sam 16:18 David; 1 Kgs 11:28 Yarav'am). The ASV-baseline 'able men' is preserved; named scholarship (Sarna, Hamilton, Wenham) documents the office-title's administrative-vs-military register-ambiguity.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֵ֤א יוֹסֵף֙ אֶת־יַֽעֲקֹ֣ב אָבִ֔יו וַיַּֽעֲמִדֵ֖הוּ לִפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וַיְבָ֥רֶךְ יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֶת־פַּרְעֹֽה׃

i18n.en: And Yosef brought in Ya'aqov his father, and set him before Pharaoh: and Ya'aqov blessed Pharaoh.

notes.official: *Va-yevarekh Ya'aqov et-Par'oh* — 'and Ya'aqov blessed Pharaoh.' One of the cycle's most-noted single phrases. The new overlay `barakh-yaaqov-blesses-pharaoh-inversion-gen47` documents the literary inversion (the subordinate blesses the sovereign) and the three named-scholarship readings without adjudicating: (a) **courtly-greeting** *barakh* — the standard ANE court-protocol salutation 'greet / give the blessing-of-greeting' (Hamilton, with reference to 1 Sam 13:10, 25:14 *le-varekh*-as-greet usage); (b) **patriarchal blessing-as-act** — the Avrahamic-promise *u-vrakhah* in its full theological-relational force, with Ya'aqov as the conduit of Gen 12:3 *u-mi-shpechot ha-adamah* (Sarna, Alter); (c) **deliberately ambiguous** — Westermann's reading that the narrator preserves both registers as overlay. The inclusio at v 10 closes the audience with the same phrase.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֖ה אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֑ב כַּמָּ֕ה יְמֵ֖י שְׁנֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: And Pharaoh said unto Ya'aqov, How many are the days of the years of thy life?

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה יְמֵי֙ שְׁנֵ֣י מְגוּרַ֔י שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וּמְאַ֖ת שָׁנָ֑ה מְעַ֣ט וְרָעִ֗ים הָיוּ֙ יְמֵי֙ שְׁנֵ֣י חַיַּ֔י וְלֹ֣א הִשִּׂ֗יגוּ אֶת־יְמֵי֙ שְׁנֵי֙ חַיֵּ֣י אֲבֹתַ֔י בִּימֵ֖י מְגוּרֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And Ya'aqov said unto Pharaoh, The days of the years of my pilgrimage are a hundred and thirty years: few and evil have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not attained unto the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage.

notes.official:
One of the corpus's most-cited single sentences — Ya'aqov's complete summation of patriarchal existence as *megurim*. Three flags:

(i) **The *megurai* / *megureihem* deployment.** The cluster's most-cited single verse; governed by the new central `megurim-patriarchal-sojourner-self-identity-gur-root`. Heb 11:13 explicitly cites the patriarchal-sojourner-self-identification here (*xenoi kai parepidemoi epi tes ges*).

(ii) **The *me'at ve-ra'im* self-assessment.** The new overlay `me-at-ve-ra-im-few-and-evil-yaaqov-self-assessment-gen47` documents Ya'aqov's anthropological self-assessment as the cycle's most explicit autobiographical-reflection. Named scholarship (Sarna, Alter, Brueggemann, Westermann) reads the line as the patriarch's mature assessment of a life of *machanayim* / *peniel* / sons-lost-and-restored — without adjudicating between the 'pessimistic-self-pity' reading (von Rad) and the 'realistic-Bildungsroman-summation' reading (Alter).

(iii) **Numerology.** The 130 years here + the 17 years in Mitsrayim (v 28) = 147; tracked in the v 28 commentary via the new overlay `seventeen-seventeen-symmetry-yaaqov-yosef-numerology-gen47`.

ASV-baseline 'pilgrimage' preserved at this verse (the ASV uses 'pilgrimage' specifically at Gen 47:9; Heb 11:13 *parepidemoi* anchors the rendering).

paragraphs.text: וַיְבָ֥רֶךְ יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֶת־פַּרְעֹ֑ה וַיֵּצֵ֖א מִלִּפְנֵ֥י פַרְעֹֽה׃

i18n.en: And Ya'aqov blessed Pharaoh, and went out from the presence of Pharaoh.

notes.official: The closing-inclusio of the audience-scene: *va-yevarekh Ya'aqov et-Par'oh* — verbatim the v 7 opener. The overlay `barakh-yaaqov-blesses-pharaoh-inversion-gen47` governs both occurrences.

paragraphs.text: וַיּוֹשֵׁ֣ב יוֹסֵף֮ אֶת־אָבִ֣יו וְאֶת־אֶחָיו֒ וַיִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֤ם אֲחֻזָּה֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּמֵיטַ֥ב הָאָ֖רֶץ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ רַעְמְסֵ֑ס כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֥ה פַרְעֹֽה׃

i18n.en: And Yosef placed his father and his brethren, and gave them a possession in the land of Mitsrayim, in the best of the land, in the land of Ra'meses, as Pharaoh had commanded.

notes.official:
Two MAJOR central additions:

(i) **The *achuzzah* keyword.** *Achuzzah* (root *achaz*) is the patriarchal-land-promise institutional-term: the legal-holding / possession granted-and-held by clan-tenure. Cross-corpus saturation: Gen 17:8 *la-achuzzat olam* (the Avrahamic land-grant); 23:4+9+20 *achuzzat qever* (the Makhpelah purchase); 36:43; 48:4; 49:30; 50:13; Lev 25 Jubilee-tenure saturation; Num/Josh land-allocation; Ezek 44-48 future-land-allocation. The new central `achuzzah-patriarchal-possession-holding-keyword` governs the keyword. **The ironic tension** is documented as named literary observation: the patriarchal *achuzzah* promised in Kena'an is here received in Mitsrayim — and the chapter immediately undoes this by Ya'aqov's vv 29-30 burial-oath refusing to be buried in this *achuzzah*. Inclusio with v 27 *va-ye'achazu vah* (Niphal of the same root), governed by the new overlay `va-yeachazu-vah-achuzzah-inclusio-gen47`, bidirectionally cross-linked to the new central.

(ii) **The toponym Ra'meses.** The new central `raamses-eastern-delta-store-city-toponym` documents the Per-Ramesses / Pi-Ramesses identification (the 19th-Dynasty capital at Tell ed-Dab'a / Qantir, 13th c BCE; Bietak's excavations). Cross-corpus Exod 1:11 (the slave-built store-cities Pithom and Ra'meses), Exod 12:37 (the Exodus starting-point), Num 33:3+5. The dating-anachronism debate (Kitchen / Wenham proleptic-naming defense vs Redford / Bietak post-Ramesside redaction; the documentary-critical reading as a Priestly editorial-update) is documented without adjudication. NO theological-chronological pre-resolution.

The *be-meitav ha-aretz* identifies the *achuzzah* with the Pharaonic *chelev ha-aretz* of Gen 45:18 — the overlay `chelev-ha-aretz-best-of-the-land-pharaoh-grant-gen45` is extended to GEN-WOH-47:6 + 47:11.

paragraphs.text: וַיְכַלְכֵּ֤ל יוֹסֵף֙ אֶת־אָבִ֣יו וְאֶת־אֶחָ֔יו וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑יו לֶ֖חֶם לְפִ֥י הַטָּֽף׃

i18n.en: And Yosef nourished his father, and his brethren, and all his father's household, with bread, according to their families.

notes.official:
The cycle's *kalkel*-arc reaches its perfective-fulfilment node. The overlay `kalkel-yosef-sustenance-promise-gen45-46-47-50` (whose existing rationale already names this verse explicitly as the 47:12 fulfilment of the 45:11 promise *ve-khilkalti otkha sham*) has `appliesTo` extended to GEN-WOH-47:12. The cycle arc: Gen 45:11 (futuric promise) → Gen 47:12 (here, perfective fulfilment) → Gen 50:21 (post-Ya'aqov-death repetition *anokhi achalkel etkhem*).

The *taph* dependents-class noun (governed by the existing overlay `taph-little-ones-dependents-class-yosef-cycle-gen46`) has `appliesTo` extended to GEN-WOH-47:12 (here) and GEN-WOH-47:24 (the famine-policy reservation of grain *le-ekhol le-tappekhem*). The construction *lechem le-fi ha-taph* — 'bread according to the mouth-count of the little-ones / by the household-size' — is the cycle's distributive-formula by dependents-count.

paragraphs.text: וְלֶ֤חֶם אֵין֙ בְּכָל־הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּֽי־כָבֵ֥ד הָרָעָ֖ב מְאֹ֑ד וַתֵּ֜לַהּ אֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ וְאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן מִפְּנֵ֖י הָרָעָֽב׃

i18n.en: And there was no bread in all the land; for the famine was very sore, so that the land of Mitsrayim and the land of Kena'an fainted by reason of the famine.

notes.official:
The chapter pivots into the famine-policy passage (vv 13-26). Two flags:

(i) **The rare *va-telah*.** The verb *lahah* is a hapax in this form; cognates suggest 'be exhausted / faint / languish' (Prov 26:18 the Hitpael *ke-mitlahleha* 'like a maniac' is the closest cognate-attestation, semantically distant). The new overlay `va-telah-famine-faintness-rare-form-gen47` documents the rare-form and named-scholarship readings (HALOT, BDB, Sarna, Westermann). ASV-baseline 'fainted' preserved.

(ii) **The famine-policy reading-divide entry-point.** The new overlay `famine-policy-reading-divide-yosef-administrator-vs-enslaver-gen47` (anchored at v 13 as the policy-passage's structural-opener and applying across vv 13-26) documents the two principal scholarly readings without adjudicating: **(a) Yosef-as-benevolent-administrator** (Sarna, Hamilton, Wenham, von Rad — humanitarian crisis-management; the policy as proportionate-to-emergency); **(b) Yosef-as-enslaver-of-Mitsrayim** (Brueggemann, Levenson, modern critical readings — the policy as proto-totalitarian land-and-labor expropriation; the Mitsrim's voluntary-servitude at v 19 as the proto-Exodus-bondage that returns to Israel at Exod 1:11+13-14). Westermann and Alter document the deliberate dual-edge of the narrative. NO WoH spin on Yosef-as-administrator; the entry presents the divide as contested scholarly-literary observation only.

paragraphs.text: וַיְלַקֵּ֣ט יוֹסֵ֗ף אֶת־כָּל־הַכֶּ֙סֶף֙ הַנִּמְצָ֤א בְאֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ וּבְאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן בַּשֶּׁ֖בֶר אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֣ם שֹׁבְרִ֑ים וַיָּבֵ֥א יוֹסֵ֛ף אֶת־הַכֶּ֖סֶף בֵּ֥יתָה פַרְעֹֽה׃

i18n.en: And Yosef gathered up all the money that was found in the land of Mitsrayim, and in the land of Kena'an, for the grain which they bought: and Yosef brought the money into Pharaoh's house.

notes.official: The first famine-stage: **silver**. *Va-yelaqqet Yosef et kol ha-kesef* — 'and Yosef gathered up all the money.' The central `shever-mashbir-grain-purchase-vocabulary-yosef-cycle` `appliesTo` is extended to GEN-WOH-47:14 (the cycle's keyword recurs at its policy-passage deployment). The cycle's grain-trade vocabulary continues; the silver is the first of the three resource-stages (silver → livestock → land + bodies) that structure the *famine-policy* arc.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּתֹּ֣ם הַכֶּ֗סֶף מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַיִם֮ וּמֵאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַעַן֒ וַיָּבֹאוּ֩ כָל־מִצְרַ֨יִם אֶל־יוֹסֵ֤ף לֵאמֹר֙ הָֽבָה־לָּ֣נוּ לֶ֔חֶם וְלָ֥מָּה נָמ֖וּת נֶגְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֥י אָפֵ֖ס כָּֽסֶף׃

i18n.en: And when the money was all spent in the land of Mitsrayim, and in the land of Kena'an, all the Mitsrim came unto Yosef, and said, Give us bread: for why should we die in thy presence? for our money faileth.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹסֵף֙ הָב֣וּ מִקְנֵיכֶ֔ם וְאֶתְּנָ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם בְּמִקְנֵיכֶ֑ם אִם־אָפֵ֖ס כָּֽסֶף׃

i18n.en: And Yosef said, Give your cattle; and I will give you for your cattle, if money fail.

notes.official: The second famine-stage: **livestock**. *Havu miqneikhem* — 'give your cattle.' Within the famine-policy reading-divide overlay's scope (vv 13-26).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבִ֣יאוּ אֶת־מִקְנֵיהֶם֮ אֶל־יוֹסֵף֒ וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לָהֶם֩ יוֹסֵ֨ף לֶ֜חֶם בַּסּוּסִ֗ים וּבְמִקְנֵ֥ה הַצֹּ֛אן וּבְמִקְנֵ֥ה הַבָּקָ֖ר וּבַחֲמֹרִ֑ים וַיְנַהֲלֵ֤ם בַּלֶּ֙חֶם֙ בְּכָל־מִקְנֵהֶ֔ם בַּשָּׁנָ֖ה הַהִֽוא׃

i18n.en: And they brought their cattle unto Yosef; and Yosef gave them bread in exchange for the horses, and for the flocks, and for the herds, and for the asses: and he fed them with bread in exchange for all their cattle for that year.

notes.official: *Va-yenahalem ba-lechem* — 'and he led/fed them with bread.' The Piel of *nahal* primarily means 'lead gently, conduct (like a shepherd)' — cross-corpus the Pi'el's most-famous deployment is Ps 23:2 *al-mei menuchot yenahaleni* ('he leadeth me beside still waters') and Isa 40:11 *olot yenahel* (the shepherd-image of God leading the nursing-ewes). The new overlay `va-yenahalem-shepherd-led-with-bread-nahal-gen47` documents the chapter's extension of the shepherd-leading verb to the sustenance-distribution context (sustain-by-leading; provide-for-by-conducting). Named scholarship (HALOT, BDB, NIDOTTE; Sarna, Hamilton; the irony noted in some readings — Yosef *yenahel* the Mitsrim with bread in exchange for their *miqneh*). ASV-baseline 'fed' preserved.

paragraphs.text: וַתִּתֹּם֮ הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַהִוא֒ וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ אֵלָ֜יו בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשֵּׁנִ֗ית וַיֹּ֤אמְרוּ לוֹ֙ לֹֽא־נְכַחֵ֣ד מֵֽאֲדֹנִ֔י כִּ֚י אִם־תַּ֣ם הַכֶּ֔סֶף וּמִקְנֵ֥ה הַבְּהֵמָ֖ה אֶל־אֲדֹנִ֑י לֹ֤א נִשְׁאַר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י בִּלְתִּ֥י אִם־גְּוִיָּתֵ֖נוּ וְאַדְמָתֵֽנוּ׃

i18n.en: And when that year was ended, they came unto him the second year, and said unto him, We will not hide from my lord, how that our money is all spent; and the herds of cattle are my lord's; there is nought left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies, and our lands:

notes.official: *Gevyateinu ve-admateinu* — 'our bodies and our lands.' The new overlay `gevyateinu-bodies-as-property-gen47` documents the noun *gevyah* as a marked HB term, primarily denoting *corpse / dead-body* (Judg 14:8-9 Shimshon's lion-carcass; 1 Sam 31:10-12 Sha'ul's corpse on the wall of Bet-Shan; Ezek 1:11+23 the *chayyot*-bodies; Dan 10:6 Daniel's vision-figure; Neh 9:37 the post-exilic complaint *u-vi-gviyoteinu moshlim* — 'they have dominion over our bodies'). The use here for *living*-bodies-as-property is striking: the construction names the body as the last commodifiable resource after silver and livestock. Named scholarship (Sarna, Westermann, Hamilton; the Neh 9:37 parallel as the post-exilic complaint-echo). ASV-baseline 'bodies' preserved.

paragraphs.text: לָ֧מָּה נָמ֣וּת לְעֵינֶ֗יךָ גַּם־אֲנַ֙חְנוּ֙ גַּ֣ם אַדְמָתֵ֔נוּ קְנֵֽה־אֹתָ֥נוּ וְאֶת־אַדְמָתֵ֖נוּ בַּלָּ֑חֶם וְנִֽהְיֶ֞ה אֲנַ֤חְנוּ וְאַדְמָתֵ֙נוּ֙ עֲבָדִ֣ים לְפַרְעֹ֔ה וְתֶן־זֶ֗רַע וְנִֽחְיֶה֙ וְלֹ֣א נָמ֔וּת וְהָאֲדָמָ֖ה לֹ֥א תֵשָֽׁם׃

i18n.en: wherefore should we die before thine eyes, both we and our land? buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants unto Pharaoh: and give us seed, that we may live, and not die, and that the land be not desolate.

notes.official: The Mitsrim's voluntary-servitude declaration: *ve-nihyeh anachnu ve-admateinu avadim le-Par'oh* — 'we and our land will be servants unto Pharaoh.' Within the famine-policy reading-divide scope (vv 13-26). The enslaver-of-Mitsrayim reading reads this verse as the cycle's structural inversion: the *avadim*-status willingly accepted by the Mitsrim here returns to Israel as imposed *avdut* at Exod 1:13-14 (Levenson, Brueggemann). The benevolent-administrator reading reads the *avadim*-status as a defined tax-tenure (Sarna, Hamilton, Wenham), structurally distinct from chattel-slavery. The overlay documents the divide; the surface is neutral.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּ֨קֶן יוֹסֵ֜ף אֶת־כָּל־אַדְמַ֤ת מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ לְפַרְעֹ֔ה כִּֽי־מָכְר֤וּ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ אִ֣ישׁ שָׂדֵ֔הוּ כִּֽי־חָזַ֥ק עֲלֵהֶ֖ם הָרָעָ֑ב וַתְּהִ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ לְפַרְעֹֽה׃

i18n.en: So Yosef bought all the land of Mitsrayim for Pharaoh; for the Mitsrim sold every man his field, because the famine was sore upon them: and the land became Pharaoh's.

notes.official: The third famine-stage's land-component: *va-tehi ha-aretz le-Par'oh* — 'and the land became Pharaoh's.' The land-expropriation node within the famine-policy reading-divide.

paragraphs.text: וְאֶ֨ת־הָעָ֔ם הֶעֱבִ֥יר אֹת֖וֹ לֶעָרִ֑ים מִקְצֵ֥ה גְבוּל־מִצְרַ֖יִם וְעַד־קָצֵֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: And as for the people, he removed them to the cities from one end of the border of Mitsrayim even to the other end thereof.

notes.official: MAJOR TEXTUAL VARIANT. The MT *he'evir oto le-arim* ('he removed them to the cities' — population-relocation, Hiphil of *avar* + *arim* with *resh*) vs LXX + Samaritan Pentateuch *he'evid oto la-avadim* ('made them slaves / reduced them to bondmen' — Hiphil of *avad* + *avadim* with *dalet*). The one-letter ר/ד graphical-similarity variant is one of the famine-policy passage's structurally-most-consequential textual cruxes: the MT supports the population-relocation reading (consistent with the centralized-administration / dispossession-to-make-tenancy-explicit reading — Rashi: 'so that they might know they were dispossessed of the land'); the LXX/SP supports the enslavement reading (consistent with the enslaver-of-Mitsrayim hermeneutic). The new overlay `mt-lxx-sp-he-evir-le-arim-vs-he-evid-la-avadim-textual-variant-gen47` documents the variant per Tov, Skinner, Westermann, and the NRSV textual-notes without adjudicating. MT preserved per the project's Gen 22:13 MT-fidelity baseline.

paragraphs.text: רַ֛ק אַדְמַ֥ת הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים לֹ֣א קָנָ֑ה כִּי֩ חֹ֨ק לַכֹּהֲנִ֜ים מֵאֵ֣ת פַּרְעֹ֗ה וְאָֽכְל֤וּ אֶת־חֻקָּם֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֤ן לָהֶם֙ פַּרְעֹ֔ה עַל־כֵּ֕ן לֹ֥א מָכְר֖וּ אֶת־אַדְמָתָֽם׃

i18n.en: Only the land of the priests bought he not: for the priests had a portion from Pharaoh, and did eat their portion which Pharaoh gave them; wherefore they sold not their land.

notes.official:
The priest-exemption: the Egyptian-priesthood's land is exempt from the policy because the priests have a *choq* — a fixed allotment / ration — from Pharaoh. The new overlay `choq-allotment-vs-statute-double-deployment-gen47` documents the chapter's double-deployment of *choq* in two distinct senses within five verses: (a) v 22 *choq la-kohanim* — the older economic 'allotment / fixed-ration' sense (cf. Gen 47:22 thrice, Exod 5:14 the brick-quota, Lev 6:11 the priestly *choq*-share, Prov 30:8); (b) v 26 *va-yasem otah Yosef le-choq* — the legal-religious 'statute / decree' sense (cross-corpus saturation in Exod, Lev, Num, Deut, Pss). The chapter is one of the corpus's clearest single-passage demonstrations of the lexeme's full semantic range. ASV-baseline's distinction ('portion' at v 22 / 'statute' at v 26) preserved.

**Note on Egyptian historical-background.** The priest-exemption corresponds to known Egyptian-administrative practice of priestly land-holdings exempt from royal taxation in various periods (Vergote, Redford, Hoffmeier); the named-scholarship Egyptological observation is documented without adjudicating the broader historicity-debate.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹסֵף֙ אֶל־הָעָ֔ם הֵן֩ קָנִ֨יתִי אֶתְכֶ֥ם הַיּ֛וֹם וְאֶת־אַדְמַתְכֶ֖ם לְפַרְעֹ֑ה הֵֽא־לָכֶ֣ם זֶ֔רַע וּזְרַעְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־הָאֲדָמָֽה׃

i18n.en: Then Yosef said unto the people, Behold, I have bought you this day and your land for Pharaoh: lo, here is seed for you, and ye shall sow the land.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָה֙ בַּתְּבוּאֹ֔ת וּנְתַתֶּ֥ם חֲמִישִׁ֖ית לְפַרְעֹ֑ה וְאַרְבַּ֣ע הַיָּדֹ֡ת יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶם֩ לְזֶ֨רַע הַשָּׂדֶ֧ה וּֽלְאָכְלְכֶ֛ם וְלַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּבָתֵּיכֶ֖ם וְלֶאֱכֹ֥ל לְטַפְּכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And it shall come to pass at the ingatherings, that ye shall give a fifth unto Pharaoh, and four parts shall be your own, for seed of the field, and for your food, and for them of your households, and for food for your little ones.

notes.official:
The famine-policy implementation: the **fifth-share** (*chamishit*) becomes the permanent post-famine tax-rate. The overlay `chimmesh-fifth-part-or-fifth-division-gen41` (whose existing rationale already extensively documents the Gen 41:34 *chimmesh* / Gen 47:24+26 *chamishit/chomesh* policy-initiation-to-permanent-codification arc) has `appliesTo` extended to GEN-WOH-47:24 + 47:26 to formalize the Gen 41 ↔ Gen 47 cycle-internal narrative-fulfilment arc — one of the cycle's neatest policy-arc structures.

The *taph* dependents-class noun (`taph-little-ones-dependents-class-yosef-cycle-gen46`) is extended to include this verse's *le-ekhol le-tappekhem* (the household-distributive remainder).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ הֶחֱיִתָ֑נוּ נִמְצָא־חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י וְהָיִ֥ינוּ עֲבָדִ֖ים לְפַרְעֹֽה׃

i18n.en: And they said, Thou hast saved our lives: let us find favor in the sight of my lord, and we will be servants unto Pharaoh.

notes.official:
Two flags:

(i) **The *hechiyitanu* Hiphil.** The Hiphil of *chayah* — 'thou hast saved our lives / preserved us alive' — verbally echoes the cycle's central preservation-of-life thread: Gen 45:5 *le-michyah* (the providential-purpose noun, governed by central `michyah-preservation-of-life-rare-noun`); Gen 45:7 *le-hachayot lakhem* (the expanded-providential-purpose Hiphil-infinitive). The central `michyah-preservation-of-life-rare-noun` has `appliesTo` extended to GEN-WOH-47:25 + rationale extended to document the Mitsrim's adoption of the Yosef-cycle's preservation-of-life vocabulary as the famine-policy's literary closure: the same *chayah*-arc that names Yosef's mission (45:5) is here applied by the Mitsrim to Yosef's policy. This wires a cross-link to the Gen 45 overlay `va-techi-ruach-yaaqov-spirit-revival-chayah-arc-gen45` (whose rationale is extended to note the v 47:25 closure of the cycle's chayah-arc).

(ii) **The *matza chen be-einei X* formula.** The new central `matza-chen-be-einei-x-favor-formula` documents the corpus-saturating courtly-deference formula: Gen 6:8 (Noach), 18:3, 19:19, 30:27, 32:6, 33:8+10+15, 34:11, 39:4+21, 47:25 (here), 47:29 (Ya'aqov to Yosef), 50:4; saturation across Exod 33, Num, Ruth, 1-2 Sam. The chapter deploys the formula twice (vv 25 and 29), framing the famine-policy closure and the burial-oath request.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֣שֶׂם אֹתָ֣הּ יוֹסֵ֡ף לְחֹק֩ עַד־הַיּ֨וֹם הַזֶּ֜ה עַל־אַדְמַ֥ת מִצְרַ֛יִם לְפַרְעֹ֖ה לַחֹ֑מֶשׁ רַ֞ק אַדְמַ֤ת הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ לְבַדָּ֔ם לֹ֥א הָיְתָ֖ה לְפַרְעֹֽה׃

i18n.en: And Yosef made it a statute concerning the land of Mitsrayim unto this day, that Pharaoh should have the fifth; only the land of the priests alone became not Pharaoh's.

notes.official:
MAJOR central addition: **the *ad ha-yom ha-zeh* editorial-aetiological formula.** *Va-yasem otah Yosef le-choq ad ha-yom ha-zeh* — 'and Yosef made it a statute unto this day.' The new central `ad-ha-yom-ha-zeh-aetiological-formula` documents the corpus-saturating signature-formula of the deuteronomistic editorial-tradition. Cross-corpus saturation: Gen 19:37+38, 22:14, 26:33, 32:33, 35:20, 47:26 (here), 48:15, 50:11 (the Genesis-internal instances); Deut 2:22, 3:14, 10:8, 11:4, 29:3, 34:6; Josh 4:9, 5:9, 6:25, 7:26, 8:28+29, 9:27, 10:27, 13:13, 14:14, 15:63, 16:10, 22:3+17; saturation across Judg, 1-2 Sam, 1-2 Kgs, 1-2 Chr. Named scholarship: Brevard Childs's classic 'A Study of the Formula 'Until This Day'' (JBL 82, 1963) — the standard treatment; Childs *Introduction to the OT as Scripture* 1979; Lemche, Van Seters on the J / Dtr source-critical readings; the documentary-critical observation of the formula as the editorial signature of an institutional-aetiology. NO theological-pre-resolution; the entry presents the named-scholarly observation without adjudicating between the J-Yahwist-attribution, the Dtr-editorial-attribution, and the Priestly-redactional-layer attribution.

The chapter's institutional-aetiology is precise: Yosef's famine-policy is being named as an enduring legal-institution. The *le-choq* deployment at this verse pairs with the v 22 *choq la-kohanim* (allotment-sense) — see the overlay `choq-allotment-vs-statute-double-deployment-gen47`. The Gen 41 → Gen 47 *chimmesh* policy-arc (initiation → permanent-codification) is the central institutional-thread: `chimmesh-fifth-part-or-fifth-division-gen41` extended to GEN-WOH-47:24 + 47:26.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם בְּאֶ֣רֶץ גֹּ֑שֶׁן וַיֵּאָחֲז֣וּ בָ֔הּ וַיִּפְר֥וּ וַיִּרְבּ֖וּ מְאֹֽד׃

i18n.en: And Yisra'el dwelt in the land of Mitsrayim, in the land of Goshen; and they got them possessions therein, and were fruitful and multiplied exceedingly.

notes.official:
The chapter's structural inclusio-and-Exodus-bridge verse. Three flags:

(i) **The *peru u-rvu* creation-blessing fulfilment-thread.** *Va-yifru va-yirbu me'od* — an explicit echo of Gen 1:22+28 (creation), Gen 9:1+7 (post-Flood), and the patriarchal-blessing repetitions (Gen 17:6+20, 28:3, 35:11, 48:4). The central `peru-urvu` (Gen 1:22, 1:28, 35:11) has `appliesTo` extended to GEN-WOH-47:27, with rationale extension documenting the patriarchal-and-Egypt-period fulfilment-thread (Cassuto, Sarna, Westermann on the blessing-formula; Brueggemann on the formula as covenant-of-creation; the Yosef-cycle / Exodus thematic-bridge to Exod 1:7 *u-vnei Yisra'el paru va-yishretzu va-yirbu va-ya'atzmu bi-me'od me'od* — the verbatim continuation that opens the Exodus narrative). The decision to extend `peru-urvu` (rather than create a new central) preserves the architectural-decision that the patriarchal-blessing repetitions are continuous with the Gen 1 creation-blessing; the related entry `peru-urevu-postflood` (Gen 9:1, 9:7) remains scoped to the post-Flood pair. NO theological-typological adjudication.

(ii) **The *va-ye'achazu vah* inclusio.** The Niphal *va-ye'achazu* — 'they got them possessions / they took hold therein' — is the verbal-cognate of the v 11 *achuzzah* (root *achaz*). The new overlay `va-yeachazu-vah-achuzzah-inclusio-gen47` documents the chapter-internal noun-verb inclusio (v 11 noun *achuzzah* → v 27 verb *va-ye'achazu*) and is **bidirectionally cross-linked** to the new central `achuzzah-patriarchal-possession-holding-keyword`. The ironic-tension is preserved: the patriarchal *achuzzah*-keyword promised in Kena'an is here received in Mitsrayim — and the chapter immediately undoes this by Ya'aqov's vv 29-30 burial-oath.

(iii) **Goshen extension.** The central `goshen-egyptian-province-eastern-delta-toponym` `appliesTo` is extended to GEN-WOH-47:27 (the chapter's fourth Goshen-occurrence).

paragraphs.text: וַיְחִ֤י יַעֲקֹב֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם שְׁבַ֥ע עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה וַיְהִ֤י יְמֵֽי־יַעֲקֹב֙ שְׁנֵ֣י חַיָּ֔יו שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים וּמְאַ֖ת שָׁנָֽה׃

i18n.en: And Ya'aqov lived in the land of Mitsrayim seventeen years: so the days of Ya'aqov, the years of his life, were a hundred and forty and seven years.

notes.official: **The 17/17/147 numerology.** The new overlay `seventeen-seventeen-symmetry-yaaqov-yosef-numerology-gen47` documents the named-scholarship literary-architectural observation: Yosef was sold at 17 (Gen 37:2 *ben sheva-esreh shanah*); Ya'aqov dwells in Mitsrayim 17 years (here); Ya'aqov's total life is 147 years. The Sarna / Alter symmetry-of-life observation (17 years of Ya'aqov-with-Yosef-as-son in Kena'an before the loss + 17 years of Ya'aqov-with-Yosef-as-Egyptian-ruler in Mitsrayim after the recovery) is documented; the Cassuto numerological-pattern reading (147 = 3 × 7² = the patriarch's perfect-number-product; cf. Avraham's 175 = 7 × 5², Yitzchaq's 180 = 5 × 6²) is documented; the Westermann skeptical position (numerology overread) is documented. No adjudication.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרְב֣וּ יְמֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֘ל לָמוּת֒ וַיִּקְרָ֣א ׀ לִבְנ֣וֹ לְיוֹסֵ֗ף וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ אִם־נָ֨א מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ שִֽׂים־נָ֥א יָדְךָ֖ תַּ֣חַת יְרֵכִ֑י וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ עִמָּדִי֙ חֶ֣סֶד וֶאֱמֶ֔ת אַל־נָ֥א תִקְבְּרֵ֖נִי בְּמִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And the time drew near that Yisra'el must die: and he called his son Yosef, and said unto him, If now I have found favor in thy sight, put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh, and deal kindly and truly with me: bury me not, I pray thee, in Mitsrayim;

notes.official:
The deathbed-prep scene gathers four governed formulae:

(i) **The *matza chen be-einei X* formula.** Second deployment of the chapter (after v 25). Governed by the new central `matza-chen-be-einei-x-favor-formula`.

(ii) **The oath-thigh gesture.** *Sim-na yadkha tachat yerekhi* — 'put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh.' The only other HB attestation of the oath-thigh-gesture is Gen 24:2+9 (Avraham's servant for Yitzchaq's wife). The existing central `yad-tachat-yarekh-oath-gesture` has its `appliesTo` corrected from the legacy `GEN-47:29` form to `GEN-WOH-47:29` (the entry already names this verse).

(iii) **The *chesed ve-emet* formula.** *Va-asita immadi chesed ve-emet* — the patriarchal covenantal-formulaic-pair. The existing central `chesed-v-emet-steadfast-love-and-truth` (Gen 24:27, 24:49, 32:11) has `appliesTo` extended to GEN-WOH-47:29 (the cycle's principal deathbed deployment).

(iv) **The burial-refusal of Mitsrayim.** *Al-na tiqbreni be-Mitsrayim* — 'bury me not, I pray thee, in Mitsrayim.' The patriarchal *achuzzah*-tension reaches its narrative-resolution here: the *achuzzah* received in Mitsrayim (v 11) is rejected as a burial-place; the *achuzzat qever* of Gen 23:4+9+20 (the Makhpelah-tomb) is named as the burial-destination at v 30. The new central `achuzzah-patriarchal-possession-holding-keyword` rationale documents this Gen 47:11 ↔ Gen 47:29-30 ↔ Gen 23 narrative-architecture.

paragraphs.text: וְשָֽׁכַבְתִּי֙ עִם־אֲבֹתַ֔י וּנְשָׂאתַ֙נִי֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וּקְבַרְתַּ֖נִי בִּקְבֻרָתָ֑ם וַיֹּאמַ֕ר אָנֹכִ֖י אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֥ה כִדְבָרֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: but when I sleep with my fathers, thou shalt carry me out of Mitsrayim, and bury me in their burying-place. And he said, I will do as thou hast said.

notes.official: MAJOR central addition: the **death-formula** *shakhav im-avotav*. The new central `shakhav-im-avotav-death-formula` documents this Gen 47:30 occurrence as the corpus's earliest attestation of what becomes the deuteronomistic-Kings signature death-notice formula. Cross-corpus saturation: Gen 47:30 (here), Gen 49:29+33 (Ya'aqov's death proper); Deut 31:16 (Mosheh's projected death + the people's apostasy-warning); 2 Sam 7:12 (the Davidic-covenant context — *ve-shakhavta et-avoteikha*); 1 Kgs 1:21, 2:10 (David), 11:21+43 (Shelomoh), 14:20+31 (Yarav'am + Rechav'am), 15:8+24 (Aviyah + Asa), 16:6+28 (Ba'sha + Omri), 22:40+51 (Ach'av + Yehoshafat); 2 Kgs 8:24, 10:35, 13:9+13, 14:16+22+29, 15:7+22+38, 16:20, 20:21, 21:18, 24:6 (the Kings-of-Israel/Judah death-notices); 2 Chr parallels. Named scholarship: Wenham on the Genesis instances; Alfrink 'L'expression שכב עם אבותיו' OTS 2 (1943); Driver, Skinner, Westermann on the formula's death-as-rest register; the deuteronomistic-Kings formulaic-pattern documented by Noth, Cross, Halpern, Friedman. NO theological-pre-resolution on the formula's afterlife-implication.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִשָּֽׁבְעָה֙ לִ֔י וַיִּשָּׁבַ֖ע ל֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ הַמִּטָּֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And he said, Swear unto me: and he sware unto him. And Yisra'el bowed himself upon the bed's head.

notes.official:
Two flags:

(i) **The cycle's last *hishtachavah*.** *Va-yishtachu Yisra'el al-rosh ha-mittah* — 'and Yisra'el bowed himself upon the bed's head.' The verbal-form completes the cycle's *hishtachavah*-arc that opened with the brothers' obeisance-in-the-sheaves-dream (Gen 37:7) and ran through 37:9+10, 42:6, 43:26+28, 44:14. The central `hishtachavah-bow-down-obeisance-worship` has `appliesTo` extended to GEN-WOH-47:31. (The named-scholarship observation: Ya'aqov here bows to the dying-father's bed in self-acknowledgment of Yosef's secured-oath — a structural mirror-and-inversion of the Gen 37 dream-sequence; Sarna, Alter, Coats.)

(ii) **MAJOR TEXTUAL VARIANT.** MT *ha-mittah* (הַמִּטָּה, 'the bed') vs LXX *tes rabdou autou* ('his staff', evidently vocalizing the same consonants as הַמַּטֶּה, 'the staff'). Heb 11:21 cites the verse with the LXX form (one of the NT's most-cited Genesis LXX-vs-MT divergences). The new overlay `mt-lxx-mittah-mateh-bed-vs-staff-textual-variant-gen47` documents the consonant-identical-vocalization variant per Tov, Skinner, Wevers, Westermann, Hamilton, NRSV textual-notes; the Heb 11:21 NT-tradition; the Targum Onqelos following the MT. MT preserved per the project's Gen 22:13 MT-fidelity baseline.
